description: The economic factors news are scored on. sentiment > 0 means the factor itself goes up, as stated in 'positive' (more growth, more inflation, tighter policy, more stress). group and region tag related factors: exposures of an asset are shrunk toward its group, and a factor without a proxy borrows its group's exposures until it has enough news. proxy is the factor's weekly market return, a sum of terms [series, transform, weight]: series 'fred:<id>' (downloaded from FRED) or 'price:<symbol>' (prices table); transform 'logret' (log return) or 'diff' (change, for yields, spreads and indices). The proxies are orthogonalized in the order of this list, so each one is its factor's shock net of the factors before it (e.g. the 2-year yield net of equities = a monetary-policy shock, Brent net of growth = energy supply, breakevens net of growth and energy = inflation).

GROWTH_US.name: US growth
GROWTH_US.positive: stronger US activity, jobs, consumer, housing

GROWTH_CHINA.name: Chinese growth
GROWTH_CHINA.positive: stronger Chinese activity, stimulus, property stabilizing

GROWTH_EM.name: Emerging-market growth
GROWTH_EM.positive: stronger emerging economies (ex China), capital inflows

TECH_AI.name: Technology and AI cycle
TECH_AI.positive: stronger AI capex, semiconductor and cloud demand

EARNINGS.name: Corporate earnings
EARNINGS.positive: earnings or guidance above expectations, margins up

POLICY_FED.name: Federal Reserve policy
POLICY_FED.positive: hawkish Fed: hikes, fewer cuts, balance-sheet tightening

POLICY_BOJ.name: Bank of Japan policy
POLICY_BOJ.positive: BoJ tightening: hikes, less bond buying

POLICY_PBOC.name: People's Bank of China policy
POLICY_PBOC.positive: PBoC tightening: less easing, higher rates or reserve ratios

POLICY_OTHER_DM.name: Other developed central banks
POLICY_OTHER_DM.positive: hawkish BoE, SNB, BoC, RBA and others

FISCAL_US.name: US fiscal policy
FISCAL_US.positive: wider deficits, more Treasury issuance, debt-ceiling stress

SOVEREIGN_EUROPE.name: European sovereign risk
SOVEREIGN_EUROPE.positive: budget or debt stress in euro-area countries, wider spreads

ENERGY_SUPPLY.name: Energy supply tightness
ENERGY_SUPPLY.positive: tighter oil and gas supply: OPEC+ cuts, outages, sanctions, inventory draws

AGRICULTURE.name: Agricultural supply tightness
AGRICULTURE.positive: tighter grain and soft-commodity supply: weather, export bans

INFLATION_US.name: US inflation
INFLATION_US.positive: higher or upside-surprising US prices and wages

INFLATION_EUROPE.name: European inflation
INFLATION_EUROPE.positive: higher or upside-surprising euro-area and UK prices

BANKING_STRESS.name: Banking and funding stress
BANKING_STRESS.positive: bank troubles, funding or liquidity squeezes

RISK_APPETITE.name: Investor risk appetite
RISK_APPETITE.positive: investors adding risk: inflows, leverage, speculation

USD.name: US dollar
USD.positive: stronger dollar against the other major currencies

JPY.name: Japanese yen
JPY.positive: stronger yen: repatriation, carry unwind, intervention

GOLD_DEMAND.name: Gold demand
GOLD_DEMAND.positive: central-bank buying, ETF inflows, safe-haven demand for gold

GEOPOLITICS.name: Geopolitical risk
GEOPOLITICS.positive: more armed conflict, sanctions, political crises

TRADE_POLICY.name: Trade policy escalation
TRADE_POLICY.positive: more tariffs, export controls, trade escalation
